questions.text: According to Kamila's blog, naming your feelings:
questions.hint: Reading 1, paragraph 5: "the emotion becomes smaller."

questions.text: Kamila felt only happiness and excitement during her first week at WKU.
questions.hint: She also felt overwhelmed — too many new things at once.

questions.text: What is "empathy" according to reading 2?
questions.hint: Paragraph 3: "empathy (understanding others)".

questions.text: Dr. Akhmetov says students with high EQ are better at:
opts: Group projects and listening to others
questions.correct: Group projects and listening to others
questions.hint: Reading 2, paragraph 4: "Students who develop EQ do better in group projects."

questions.text: Emotional intelligence is not fixed — it ___ with practice.
questions.hint: Reading 2, paragraph 6: "it grows with practice."

questions.text: Gulnaz loves learning about:
questions.hint: Listening statement 4: she loves learning about why people feel different emotions.

questions.text: Amir enjoys watching sad films to help him understand emotions.
questions.hint: He avoids sad films — they make him feel low.

questions.text: What does Kamila hope to do one day?
opts: Write a book about student mental health
questions.correct: Write a book about student mental health
questions.hint: Listening statement 6: "She hopes to write a book about student mental health."

questions.text: Amir said he hates feeling:
questions.hint: Statement 2: "He hates feeling confused — he prefers to know exactly what to do."

questions.text: Gulnaz said she enjoys ___ books about emotions and psychology.
questions.hint: enjoy + -ing: "enjoys reading".

questions.text: Which verb is followed by -ing (gerund)?
questions.hint: avoid + -ing: "avoid making mistakes". Others take to + infinitive.

questions.text: She finished ___ (write) her essay late last night.
questions.hint: finish + -ing: "finished writing".

questions.text: "She wants ___ English." Fill in:
questions.hint: want + to + infinitive.

questions.text: "I don't mind to help" is correct.
questions.hint: mind + -ing: "I don't mind helping." Not "to help".

questions.text: Which is correct?
questions.hint: hope + to + infinitive.

questions.text: Keep ___ (practise) — you're getting better every day!
questions.hint: keep + -ing: "keep practising".

questions.text: Fill in both: "She enjoys ___ but she needs ___ harder."
questions.hint: enjoy + -ing; need + to + infinitive.

questions.text: Which verb takes TO + infinitive?
questions.hint: plan + to + infinitive: "I plan to go." Others use -ing.

questions.text: He offered ___ (carry) her bags to the dormitory.
questions.hint: offer + to + infinitive.

questions.text: "She decided starting a new hobby" is correct.
questions.hint: decide + to + infinitive: "She decided to start a new hobby."

questions.text: "Overwhelmed" means:
opts: Feeling too much to cope with
questions.correct: Feeling too much to cope with
questions.hint: "Overwhelmed" = having more to deal with than you can manage.

questions.text: "Anxious" is closest in meaning to:
questions.hint: "Anxious" = nervous or worried, especially about something in the future.

questions.text: "Empathy" means only thinking about yourself.
questions.hint: "Empathy" = understanding and sharing the feelings of others — the opposite of selfishness.

questions.text: She showed great ___ — she understood exactly how I was feeling.
questions.hint: "Empathy" = the ability to understand and share someone's feelings.

questions.text: "Self-awareness" means:
opts: Being aware of your own emotions and behaviour
questions.correct: Being aware of your own emotions and behaviour
questions.hint: "Self-awareness" = knowing and understanding your own character, feelings, and behaviour.

questions.text: "Frustration" is a feeling you get when:
opts: You feel proud of your results
Things don't go as expected or hoped
questions.correct: Things don't go as expected or hoped
questions.hint: "Frustration" = annoyance or upset caused by obstacles or things not working out.

questions.text: "Confidence" means being unsure of yourself.
questions.hint: "Confidence" = the feeling of being certain about your abilities or qualities.

questions.text: "Loneliness" is the feeling of:
opts: Being alone and unhappy about it
questions.correct: Being alone and unhappy about it
questions.hint: "Loneliness" = sadness because you have no friends or company.

questions.text: "Perspective" is:
opts: A way of seeing or understanding something
A grammar term for verb tense
questions.correct: A way of seeing or understanding something
questions.hint: "Perspective" = a particular attitude or point of view toward something.

questions.text: She felt ___ when she finally graduated — all the hard work was worth it.
questions.hint: "Proud" = pleased and satisfied with something you have achieved.
